heading: INT. CARDIAC ICU - NURSES' STATION - 4 A.M.

units.text: INT. CARDIAC ICU - NURSES' STATION - 4 A.M.
A glass-walled island among curtained bays.
Monitors beep in a soft, uneven chorus.
A whiteboard lists names and numbers in four colours of marker.
Coffee grows a skin in a paper cup.
The corridor lights are dimmed to the colour of weak tea.
NURSE ROSALEEN ADEKUNLE-MARSH, fifties, in navy scrubs and compression socks, sits at a terminal, reading glasses pushed up into grey-streaked hair.
She is a veteran, lined and unhurried, who has done this shift a thousand times.
A name tag on her lanyard reads R. ADEKUNLE.
A dictation recorder lies by her keyboard, its red light steady.
She presses the button.
Four-ten. Mr. Dacosta. Stable overnight, pressure holding, no events. Four-twelve. Mrs. Lindahl. Sleeping.
units.name: ROSALEEN

units.text: She releases the button.
A monitor chirps.
She does not look up.
She sips cold coffee, grimaces, sets the cup down.
A call light blinks over bay six.
She glances at it.
Watches it blink.
Turns back to the screen, and types for a moment, and the light blinks on.
Finally she rises, and her knees pop.
She walks to the bay.
Looks in.
A man sleeps with his mouth open.
The chart at his feet is in order.
She straightens his blanket by half an inch.
Back at the station, she presses the recorder again.
Four-fourteen. Called at four-oh-six. No complaint. Repositioned. Resting.
units.name: ROSALEEN

units.text: She stops.
Listens.
The corridor is quiet.
A faint voice drifts from the intercom on the wall.
Four-ten. Mr. Dacosta. Stable overnight...
units.name: ROSALEEN

units.text: She frowns.
The recorder is still running, but she has not touched it.
She picks it up, thumbs the rewind.
Her own voice, tinny, fills the air.
Four-fourteen. Called at four-oh-six.
units.name: ROSALEEN

units.text: A longer pause.
Then, under her own voice, almost lost in the hiss, a second recording she does not remember making.
Rosaleen? It's cold in here.
units.name: ROSALEEN

units.text: She stops the tape.
The ward is silent.
She looks at the dark corridor and the bay doors and all the blinking lights, and for a long moment she doesn't move.
Then she takes off her glasses and wipes them on her sleeve.
Long night.
units.name: ROSALEEN

units.text: She puts the recorder in her pocket and walks the length of the ward, checking each bay in turn.
